propositions: The mcp entrypoint skips re-cloning if .git exists, even when HEAD is unresolvable or .git is corrupted by an interrupted clone, permanently poisoning the named volume.
A poisoned tracker directory (with or without .git) returns false-empty reads (count=0) because the store_uninitialized guard only checks directory existence, not git repository validity.
The entrypoint must verify HEAD is resolvable before trusting the clone, and clear the directory before re-cloning to prevent partial objects from blocking subsequent clones.
Concurrent provisioning windows must serialize re-clone attempts with flock on the tracker directory inode to prevent interleaved clear-and-clone operations.
A failed clone must surface in exit status rather than being suppressed, and a PAT-less boot must neither clear nor clone the store.
